title: Fine-grained lock
points: Use a separate lock per resource (per seat, per account) so threads working on different resources run in parallel.
It gives higher throughput than a coarse lock when you can partition by resource.
The cost is overhead and complexity, and the risk of deadlock when one operation needs several locks.
trade: Use it when contention matters and state can be partitioned by resource. Versus coarse: more throughput, more bugs. Avoid deadlock by always acquiring locks in a consistent global order (e.g. by id).
test: Transfers between accounts each lock both accounts. Thread 1 does A to B and thread 2 does B to A and the app hangs. What happened and how do you prevent it?
answer: Deadlock: each holds one lock and waits for the other. Always acquire the locks in the same order, such as by account id.

questions.question: Which risk is specific to fine-grained locking compared with a coarse lock?
options: Deadlock from acquiring several locks in different orders
Lost updates on a single counter
questions.explanation: Multiple locks can be held in conflicting orders. Lower throughput is the coarse-lock problem.

questions.question: When does a fine-grained lock pay off?
options: Low traffic and a single shared structure
When state can be partitioned by resource and contention is a concern
questions.explanation: It needs per-resource partitioning to help. One integer suits an atomic; read-heavy suits a read-write lock.
